title: Agent-based modeling of environment-migration linkages: a review

key_points.claim: Review covers 15 ABMs of rural environment-migration linkages (21 publications), found via a Web of Science search of 508 articles. Models are mostly tropical case studies and diverse in purpose and scale.
key_points.evidence_quote: we reviewed 15 ABMs of environment-migration linkages in rural contexts to synthesize the current state of the art

key_points.claim: The paper proposes a framework that classifies social-ecological couplings as one-way, partly integrated, or fully integrated two-way. Sugarscape variants illustrate the classes.
key_points.evidence_quote: Fully integrated two-way linkages imply that environmental consequences of natural resource use and migration decisions are considered within the model

key_points.claim: Model purposes: all models are used for system understanding. Four are used in participatory contexts, three for decision support and three for predicting migrant numbers.
key_points.evidence_quote: All considered ABMs are used for gaining system understanding

key_points.claim: Temporal scales range from 3 years with daily steps to 10,000 years with yearly steps. Some models mix time steps across processes. Spatial scales range from local to national.
key_points.evidence_quote: three years in daily time steps in Naqvi and Rehm (2014), to large, e.g., 10,000 years in yearly time steps in Janssen (2010)

key_points.claim: Environment representation: agents often affect natural resource availability. They rarely affect the influencing environmental factors, such as climate drivers.
key_points.evidence_quote: human agents affecting influencing environmental factors is rarely included in the models

key_points.claim: Main gaps: migration into and out of the system and temporary migration get little attention. 9 of 15 models lack fully integrated feedbacks.
key_points.evidence_quote: 9 out of 15 models lack fully integrated social-ecological feedbacks

key_points.claim: Recommends standards for documenting, analyzing and reusing ABMs (ODD+D, TRACE) and more interdisciplinary work on human decision-making.
key_points.evidence_quote: standards for developing and analyzing ABMs are needed

key_points.claim: Only a small share of migration ABMs include environmental factors. The 15 models compare with 27 migration ABMs in general reviewed by Klabunde and Willekens (2016).
key_points.evidence_quote: a substantial share of ABMs in the field of migration does not consider environmental factors

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched. It is a peer-reviewed review article in an open-access journal. Scope is narrow: migration and social-ecological systems, not artificial societies in general. I read the abstract, methods, overview and conclusion, and skimmed the rest.
